correctness.rationale: Every pendant pair has weight at least two, with equality only at (0,2). No three consecutive pairs can all be baseline because the middle zero cycle vertex would see closed-neighborhood weight two. Therefore exceptional indices hit all n cyclic length-three windows; since one index belongs to three windows, at least ceil(n/3) exceptions are necessary. Each costs at least one extra unit, giving the lower bound. The explicit residue-class constructions use exactly ceil(n/3) cycle labels one, all leaves two, no run 000 and no run 111, and satisfy every constrained closed neighborhood. Independent computation matches the formula in all tested orders.

value.rationale: Sunlet graphs are a standard unicyclic corona family. The exact formula reveals a structural periodic surcharge beyond the unavoidable weight-two cost per pendant pair, and the ceil(n/3) term is forced by a clean cyclic covering obstruction. This supplies a natural infinite-family benchmark for a recently introduced NP-hard domination invariant and is not merely a small-instance computation.
